migration_138_analysis.content: DEFINE FIELD OVERWRITE created_at ON execution_trace_content TYPE option<datetime> VALUE $value OR time::now();
migration_138_analysis.what_was_broken: VALUE default on DEFINE FIELD doesn't fire on INSERT INTO in this SurrealDB version. When caller omits created_at, the field gets NONE, causing 'Found NONE for field created_at' on every execution_trace_content write. This was a non-fatal but logged error on every trace.
migration_138_analysis.fix_mirrors: Mirrors migration 133 (stored_at on same table). Both fields had the same problem; 133 fixed stored_at, 138 fixes created_at.
migration_138_analysis.impact_on_thompson: Reduced error noise on trace writes, but the real Thompson fix is the normalizeActivityId() call in posterior-update.ts, not this migration.

thompson_fix_analysis.what_was_broken: Prior to this fix, rawActivityId was used directly in WHERE clause: 'WHERE variant_id = $activity_id'. If the incoming trace had activity_id='activity:⟨coverage-tick⟩' but variant_performance_metrics stored 'coverage-tick', the UPDATE matched 0 rows, leaving posteriors at their initial values forever. This explains all the 0-update observations across 100+ executions in prior investigations (F-037).
thompson_fix_analysis.fix_mechanism: normalizeActivityId() strips the 'activity:⟨⟩' wrapper. After the fix, WHERE variant_id='coverage-tick' matches the stored row and posteriors update.

These 3 failures drove beta to 2 correctly — BUT this investigation cannot confirm new post-fix executions have landed yet. The substrate restarted at ~08:50Z and only a few boredom cycles have fired.
thompson_fix_analysis.critical_caveat: The Thompson fix is in the SUBMODULE code. Whether the running container image contains this fix depends on when 'make -C scripts/substrate substrate-restart-metabob-activity-api' was last run. The submodule pointer update (4bb6ca7e) updates the source, but the container still runs the image built BEFORE the fix unless explicitly rebuilt and restarted.

findings.operator_remediation: TimeoutStartSec=300 fixed the SIGTERM issue but revealed that the boredom→goal-host HTTP call for topology goals takes > 300s. The goal-host-vessel is either hanging on the LLM call or spending too long in the execution pipeline. Consider: (a) adding request-level timeout on boredom → goal-host POST /run-goal (e.g. 60s), (b) reducing topology goal scope so execution completes under 60s, (c) checking goal-host-vessel logs for what's consuming the 300s.
